title: Brickyard retro menu cards: neutralize an 8-dish mixed-light photo batch to an in-frame grey card, author the hero + brick-sauce recolor, vectorize the wordmark, and data-merge one chalkboard card per dish
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com brief for a fast-food burger restaurant wanting a 'creative, vibrant, and appetizing' menu in a 'retro, street-food, rustic chalkboard' style with sections Classic Burgers / Specialty Burgers / Sides / Beverages, space for high-quality food photos, and deliverables as print-ready PDF (plus placeholder text/prices 'for now'). The real post names no company; the brand is laundered to the FICTIONAL retro burger joint 'Brickyard' (a generic descriptive word, not a distinctive trademark) and no other real person, brand, product, org or trademark is named. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the original implies a single from-scratch multi-item ONE-PAGE menu, which is NOT connector-doable — document_merge_data_layout emits exactly ONE FILE PER ROW (it cannot place several records on one page), and a convert_pdf_to_indd template will not bind merge fields. So the deliverable is re-cast to what the merge tool genuinely produces: a set of retro chalkboard MENU CARDS, one single-record card per dish (counter/table cards for the same four sections), which is a true one-record-per-page merge. The client supplies a genuinely hand-authored InDesign single-record menu-card template (.indd, NOT a converted PDF) carrying live <<fields>> plus THREE @-prefixed image-path columns (the per-dish photo, the shared vectorized wordmark, and the shared chalkboard texture), the dish roster as a CSV, EIGHT raw dish photos shot across busy service days under deliberately mismatched light each with a photographic 18% grey card laid in frame, and a flat wordmark scan on off-white stock. The Adobe chain does the real work the brief rewards: neutralize every dish to its own in-frame grey card so the whole set shares one warm street-food white point (each frame its own decision, not a blanket correction), carry an agent-authored hot-griddle house look built from adjustment primitives, make the flagship double-smash the hero (a masked local lift plus a masked within-family recolor of the house 'brick sauce' and a clean lift onto transparency so it floats on the chalkboard), prep-and-vectorize the scanned wordmark, source+license the chalkboard texture, then merge the authored template against the roster and export one press-ready ~300 DPI PDF, one card per dish. Placeholder copy/prices honored literally via the CSV.
one_line_ask: Neutralize eight mixed-lighting Brickyard dish photos to the 18% grey card each one carries so they read as one warm street-food set, decide each frame on its own card rather than one blanket correction, author a hot-griddle house look and make the double-smash the hero (masked local lift, masked brick-sauce recolor, clean transparent lift), prep-and-vectorize the wordmark, source a chalkboard texture, then data-merge the client's authored single-record InDesign card template to produce one press-ready chalkboard menu card per dish.
full_brief: Brickyard, a retro street-food burger joint, is printing counter and table menu cards — one card per dish across four sections (Classic Burgers, Specialty Burgers, Sides, Beverages), each in our rustic chalkboard style carrying that dish's photo, name, one-line description and placeholder price, with our wordmark crisp at the top of every card. We are NOT reshooting and we do NOT need the cards designed from scratch — we hand-built the InDesign card template ourselves. Here is the problem you are solving. We shot the eight dishes ourselves over a couple of busy service days in whatever corner of the shop was free, so straight out of the folder they do not match: some run cool, some run warm, a couple are too dark or too bright, and one or two are slightly tilted. Because we knew the light was a mess, we set a standard 18% grey card at the edge of every plate so you have something honest to balance against. Your job on the photos: make all eight read as ONE appetizing, deliberately-styled set — neutralize each frame to the grey card it carries so the whole set lands on one warm street-food white point, and make each frame its OWN decision rather than forcing one blanket correction across the batch, because each was lit differently and a fix that is right for one shot will be wrong for another. Carry a hot, punchy street-food look across the set — deep shadows, warm highlights, food that pops off the plate — but keep it believable: do not let the push turn anything muddy, orange or plasticky. When you are done, tell us the white-balance and exposure you settled on for each photo, so we can confirm the set was genuinely matched and not just eyeballed frame by frame. Make the flagship double-smash the hero of its card: lift it so it reads clearly off its cluttered background and floats cleanly on the chalkboard without a hard photographic edge, and bring our house 'brick sauce' to its proper deep brick-red on that one shot — richer and darker in the same red family — without staining the bun, the cheese or the rest of the burger. Get our wordmark razor-sharp for print. Back the cards with a rustic chalkboard/blackboard texture. Then build the cards: we are sending the dish roster and our authored menu-card template with its real placeholder fields and image slots — merge them so every dish gets its own card with its copy set, its matched photo dropped in and the crisp wordmark on top, and hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI PDF covering every dish, one card per dish. Keep every name, description and price exactly as the placeholders we send. Acceptance: every grey card reads truly neutral and the whole set sits on one white point; the hero is lifted and its sauce deepened without spilling onto the rest of the burger; the wordmark is a clean sharp vector; and there is exactly one finished card per roster row.

inputs.name: brickyard_menucard_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD retro chalkboard MENU CARD — ONE dish per page, ~5x7 in portrait at 300 DPI plus bleed. It must contain live InDesign data-merge text fields <<section>>, <<item>>, <<desc>>, <<price>> set in a chalk-white retro type treatment, and THREE @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to three separate frames: (1) a full-bleed background frame bound to @texture (the licensed chalkboard/blackboard texture), (2) a dish-photo frame stacked OVER the background bound to @dish (the matching graded dish photo — a transparent-ground PNG for the flagship so it floats on the chalkboard, an opaque rectangular photo for the others), and (3) a masthead frame at the top bound to @wordmark (the vectorized wordmark), sitting on a light distressed cream/kraft banner panel that is part of the authored card art. Built by hand in InDesign so the text fields and ALL THREE image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one dish's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template or a multi-up one-page grid would not bind / cannot be produced.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a per-dish single-record card is the correct, connector-doable shape (a single multi-item one-page menu is impossible with this tool). Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would not bind. THREE image columns (@dish per-row, @wordmark shared, @texture shared) mean the merge resolves the row's graded photo AND the shared vectorized wordmark AND the shared chalkboard texture per card, so every chain-produced asset reaches the card as a merge bind — never free-form image-at-coordinates placement (which is banned). CONSTRAINT REASONING baked into the design: the masthead panel is deliberately a LIGHT cream/kraft banner, not bare dark chalkboard, because a wordmark knocked to transparency and vectorized keeps its enclosed letter counters (in B, R, A, D) filled with the crisped ground — those read correctly on a light panel but would look wrong as filled shapes on a dark ground; so a dark-chalkboard knockout of the wordmark is intentionally NOT relied upon (mirrors the ground-truth open-counter/dark-ground rule).

inputs.name: brickyard_menu_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns section,item,desc,price,@dish,@wordmark,@texture holding EIGHT placeholder dish rows, two per section: Classic Burgers (Double Smash; Single Classic), Specialty Burgers (Bacon Jalapeno Stack; Mushroom Swiss Melt), Sides (Seasoned Fries; Beer-Batter Onion Rings), Beverages (Craft Cola; House Cold Brew). Each row carries a short appetizing one-line description and a US-dollar placeholder price (e.g. $9.50). The @dish column names the matching prepped photo file (e.g. @double_smash_hero.png for the flagship transparent hero, @single_classic.jpg for the rest) so the [T] merge drops each graded photo into that row's card. The @wordmark column holds the SAME vectorized wordmark file — @brickyard_wordmark.svg — in EVERY row, and the @texture column holds the SAME chalkboard texture file — @chalkboard_texture.jpg — in EVERY row, so the merge drops the shared masthead mark and shared background onto every card as a merge bind. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<section>>,<<item>>,<<desc>>,<<price>> and the three @image-path columns @dish,@wordmark,@texture.
inputs.realism_notes: Honors the brief's 'just use placeholder text/prices for now'; headers match the authored .indd fields and all THREE @-image columns so the one-file-per-row [T] merge binds copy, the per-dish photo, the shared wordmark AND the shared chalkboard texture per card. @wordmark and @texture carry the identical file path in all eight rows, giving the chain-produced wordmark SVG and licensed texture a connector-doable path onto every card via the merge (mirrors AO-74's shared-image-column pattern). Eight rows => the merge must produce exactly eight finished cards; row count fixes the page=row acceptance gate.

inputs.name: double_smash_hero_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless camera capture, ~4200 px on the long edge (full-resolution still straight off the camera, ~4200x2800 before crop), of a double smash burger on wax paper in a metal basket on a cluttered diner counter with ketchup bottles and napkins behind it. A photographic 18% grey card lies flat at the lower-left edge of the frame as a neutral reference. Shot under WARM tungsten diner light (strong amber cast), slightly UNDER-exposed and flat, the horizon tilted about 4 degrees. A glossy house 'brick sauce' drips from the patty stack, photographed as a dull brownish-orange under the warm light. Real sesame-seed bun texture, melted cheese drip, grease sheen, candid documentary feel, no studio gloss, no CGI. Grey card clearly visible and uncropped.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU Double Smash, the HERO / flagship (row 1, page 1). Warm tungsten + slightly under + tilted ~4deg, so it needs a cooling WB move, an exposure lift, and a straighten — its correction differs from every other frame and it is graded to establish the shared street-food white point + house look the other seven must match. THREE hero-only jobs ride on this frame: (a) a masked LOCAL lift of the burger so it reads off its cluttered surround; (b) a masked within-family recolor of the dull brownish-orange 'brick sauce' toward a deep brick-red — a small adjacent hue nudge plus a darken/desaturate that stays in the red/orange family (NO near-complementary rotation), riding the sauce's own luminosity so its sheen and folds survive, confined to the sauce so the bun/cheese are untouched; (c) a clean lift of the finished burger onto transparency so it floats on the chalkboard without a hard photo edge. Real-camera ~4200 px so every downscale to the card frame stays gen-free.

inputs.name: single_classic_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a single classic cheeseburger on a wax-paper-lined board, level framing. A photographic 18% grey card lies at the frame edge. Shot under COOL fluorescent overhead light with a distinct blue-cyan cast, normal exposure but a little flat. Real bun and patty texture, cheese pull, candid documentary feel, no CGI. Grey card clearly visible.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU Single Classic, Classic Burgers. Cool/blue fluorescent cast, level — needs WARMING to neutralize its grey card, the OPPOSITE direction from the warm hero, so a single shared white balance cannot serve both. Grey card is the neutralization target.

inputs.name: bacon_jalapeno_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a tall bacon-and-jalapeno specialty burger on a slate board, tilted about 3 degrees, lit by a MIX of cool window light on one side and warm tube light on the other so the cast is split across the frame. Normal exposure, flat contrast. A photographic 18% grey card sits at the frame edge. Real bacon, jalapeno, brioche texture, candid feel, no CGI. Grey card visible.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU Bacon Jalapeno Stack, Specialty Burgers. Split window+tube cast plus a ~3deg tilt — the hardest to neutralize; the agent must straighten it and average toward the card's neutral rather than fully killing one side, then land on the shared white point. A different correction axis again.

inputs.name: mushroom_swiss_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a mushroom-and-Swiss melt burger on a dark plate, level, lit by a single warm AMBER desk lamp, strongly warm and a touch BRIGHT. A photographic 18% grey card sits at the frame edge. Real sauteed mushroom, melted Swiss, toasted bun texture, candid feel, no CGI. Grey card visible.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU Mushroom Swiss Melt, Specialty Burgers. Strong amber cast AND slightly bright, so it needs the largest cooling WB shift of the set together with an exposure pull-DOWN — different magnitude and exposure direction from the other warm frames, proving per-frame reasoning.

inputs.name: seasoned_fries_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a basket of golden seasoned fries on a red diner tray, tilted about 4 degrees, shot against a COOL north-facing window so it runs blue and slightly flat/under. A photographic 18% grey card sits at the frame edge. Real fried texture, salt flakes, slight grease, candid documentary feel, no CGI. Grey card visible.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU Seasoned Fries, Sides. Cool north-window cast + ~4deg tilt + slightly under — warm and lift to the shared white point after straightening. A subtly different blue than the fluorescent single-classic frame, so its corrective is close but NOT equal; the agent cannot copy one cool-frame fix across both.

inputs.name: onion_rings_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a stack of beer-batter onion rings on a wax-paper-lined tray, level, lit by old overhead GREEN kitchen fluorescent tubes giving a distinct green/magenta-deficient cast, normal exposure but dull. A photographic 18% grey card sits at the frame edge. Real batter crust texture, candid feel, no CGI. Grey card visible.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU Beer-Batter Onion Rings, Sides. Green fluorescent cast needs a TINT (green->magenta) correction, not a temperature move — a different axis from the warm/cool frames; a temperature-only fix leaves the card green and fails the gate.

inputs.name: craft_cola_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a craft cola in a frosted glass bottle with condensation on a wooden counter, level, shot under NEUTRAL balanced light so the scene is already correctly white-balanced. The cola itself is a genuinely deep amber-caramel color (that warmth is the real product, not a lighting cast). A photographic 18% grey card sits at the frame edge and already reads close to neutral. Real glass reflections, water droplets, no CGI. Grey card visible.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU Craft Cola, Beverages. THE TRAP FRAME. It was shot under neutral light so its in-frame grey card is ALREADY neutral, and its warmth is the real amber cola, not a white-balance error. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (only match exposure/brightness and carry the house tonal look). A naive agent that assumes the whole batch is warm-cast and 'cools' this one chasing an imagined cast, or that batch-applies another frame's correction, will neutralize the card OFF-neutral and strip the real cola color. Decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch.

inputs.name: cold_brew_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a house cold brew over ice in a tall glass on a wooden counter, level, lit by a warm lamp and slightly OVER-exposed so the highlights on the glass and ice risk blowing out. A photographic 18% grey card sits at the frame edge. Real ice, condensation, crema, candid feel, no CGI. Grey card visible.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU House Cold Brew, Beverages. Warm AND over-exposed — cool the WB to neutralize the card and pull exposure/highlights DOWN to recover the blown glass/ice, protecting the speculars. Opposite tonal direction from the under-exposed frames, so the batch cannot share one exposure move.

inputs.name: brickyard_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'BRICKYARD' wordmark inked on off-white textured paper: a bold condensed vintage-diner slab/western display letterform, deep oxblood-red letters with a thin darker keyline. Rendered as a scan — the paper is a slightly warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 deg) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around it, and edges are a touch soft as a real scan would be. High contrast so that, once cleaned, it vectorizes crisply.
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, ~2deg skew, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize would trace the paper and the skew if fed raw — forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, crisp/raise contrast, crop to the mark, knock the off-white ground to transparency, THEN vectorize. gemini-3-pro-image for clean legible lettering. The enclosed counters (in B, R, A, D) will fill with the crisped ground on vectorize — which is why the template masthead is a LIGHT cream panel where filled counters read correctly, never a dark chalkboard knockout.

outputs.name: Brickyard_MenuCards_perDish_x8.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly eight press-ready ~5x7 in portrait retro chalkboard menu cards — ONE single-record card per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each card binds its section/item/desc/price verbatim from the roster, drops that dish's grey-card-neutralized photo into the @dish frame (the flagship as a transparent-ground PNG floating on the chalkboard, the rest as matched rectangular photos), the shared vectorized wordmark into the masthead panel via @wordmark, and the shared licensed chalkboard texture into the full-bleed background via @texture — all by merge bind, never free-form placement; ~300 DPI print quality. The flagship Double Smash is simply page 1, not a separately exported file.

outputs.name: graded_dish_photos_x8
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-neutralized, straightened dish photos delivered as the card-framed crops (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the cards via @dish — the flagship additionally lifted onto a transparent background — ALONGSIDE their RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralization is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master of each frame (its in-frame 18% grey card still present) — the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero) with the whole set matched to one shared warm street-food white point while carrying the house look; (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered card-framed crop (grey card fully cropped OUT). The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-removed crop. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance and exposure move applied to each of the eight frames. The finished flagship burger photo also doubles as a high-res social JPEG for the brand's digital use.

outputs.name: brickyard_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the BRICKYARD wordmark, traced only after the scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark, and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at masthead scale with no captured paper ground or skew. Placed on the card's light cream masthead panel (not a dark chalkboard knockout), so its enclosed letter counters read correctly.

connector_workflow.note: Search Adobe Stock for a rustic chalkboard/blackboard texture to back the menu cards (low-res candidates).
License and download the chosen chalkboard texture at full-res (license BEFORE use). Becomes the shared @texture background asset the merge drops into every card.
Triage: this frame is tilted, so level it before any grading or reframing. Only the tilted frames get straightened; the level frames skip this — deciding which is part of the job.

Establish the shared house look on the flagship and neutralize it to its own in-frame 18% grey card: reason the temperature/tint/exposure from THIS frame's card until the card reads neutral and sits at the set's shared warm street-food white point, then build the hot-griddle house tone from primitives — deep-but-uncrushed shadow floor, warm highlights, modest contrast/clarity/vibrance so the food pops without going muddy or plasticky. This is a reasoned authored grade, NOT a preset and NOT auto-tone. Report the settings applied; they define the target the other seven must match. Single primitive-built adjustments call (replaces deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _vibrance_and_saturation / _highlights).

Semantically select only the house sauce drip on the flagship burger ('the glossy sauce dripping down the patty stack') so the recolor is confined to that part and never touches the bun, cheese or the grey card. Returns a maskURI — a real object, not a hue or coordinate selection.

Masked recolor of the house sauce (consumes the graded hero + sauce mask): deepen it toward the house brick-red — a small within-family hue nudge together with a saturation/luminance drop that darkens and enriches it, staying in the red/orange family (NOT a near-complementary rotation), letting the sauce's own luminosity carry its sheen and folds. Confined to the mask so the rest of the burger is untouched. image_adjust_hsl is the ONLY masked recolor path; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image (would stain the whole burger) and image_fill_area is flat solid dead-fill (would kill the sauce sheen) — both are wrong here.

Select the burger subject so a local lift can pop it off the cluttered surround without touching the background or the grey card. Person/main-object selection is what select_subject supports; returns a maskURI.

Masked selective edit: apply a small exposure/clarity/vibrance lift to the burger subject ONLY (via the step-7 mask) so it reads off the surround, while the shadow floor and surround set in step 4 are left untouched. image_apply_adjustments accepts a mask, so this is a genuine local edit — not a whole-image push that would also lift the background.

Crop the finished flagship to the card's dish-frame ratio, framing on the food with the grey card cropped OUT — this card-removed crop is what will be lifted to transparency and bound into the card. The pre-crop neutralized master (hero_neutral, grey card still in frame) is RETAINED by the harness as the neutrality-grading artifact; the card's neutrality is graded THERE, never on this crop, and card-exclusion is the separate check on this crop. Downscale-only, onSubjectClipping='extract', never canvas-extend/upscale.

Lift the finished flagship burger onto a transparent background so it floats on the chalkboard card without a hard photographic edge. remove_background isolates the outer background only (an outer-ground knockout, no enclosed interior holes claimed); produces the transparent-ground @dish asset for row 1. This is the connector-legal path — NOT select_subject->invert->fill_area.

Neutralize this dish to its own in-frame 18% grey card and carry the shared house look established on the flagship: reason the temperature/tint/exposure from THIS frame's card to land it on the set's shared white point rather than reusing another frame's numbers, then apply the house tonal shape. Report the settings applied.

Crop the neutralized frame to the card dish-frame ratio, grey card cropped OUT; the pre-crop master (single_classic_neutral, card in frame) is retained for neutrality grading. Downscale-only, onSubjectClipping='extract'.
This frame is tilted — level it before grading.

Neutralize this dish to its own in-frame grey card and carry the shared house look: reason the white-balance/exposure from THIS frame's card to the shared white point, then apply the house tone. Report the settings applied.
Crop to the card dish-frame ratio, grey card cropped OUT; pre-crop master (bacon_neutral) retained for neutrality grading. Downscale-only, onSubjectClipping='extract'.

Neutralize this dish to its own in-frame grey card and carry the shared house look: reason the white-balance/exposure from THIS frame's card to the shared white point, then apply the house tone. Report the settings applied.
Crop to the card dish-frame ratio, grey card cropped OUT; pre-crop master (mushroom_neutral) retained for neutrality grading. Downscale-only, onSubjectClipping='extract'.
This frame is tilted — level it before grading.

Neutralize this dish to its own in-frame grey card and carry the shared house look: reason the white-balance/exposure from THIS frame's card to the shared white point, then apply the house tone. Report the settings applied.
Crop to the card dish-frame ratio, grey card cropped OUT; pre-crop master (fries_neutral) retained for neutrality grading. Downscale-only, onSubjectClipping='extract'.

Neutralize this dish to its own in-frame grey card and carry the shared house look: reason the correction from THIS frame's card to the shared white point (the residual cast here may sit on the tint axis, not temperature), then apply the house tone. Report the settings applied.
Crop to the card dish-frame ratio, grey card cropped OUT; pre-crop master (onion_neutral) retained for neutrality grading. Downscale-only, onSubjectClipping='extract'.

Neutralize this dish to its own in-frame grey card and carry the shared house look. Read THIS frame's card and let it decide the move — do not assume the batch's dominant cast applies here; match exposure/brightness to the set and hold the house tone. Report the settings applied (including if white balance was held).
Crop to the card dish-frame ratio, grey card cropped OUT; pre-crop master (cola_neutral) retained for neutrality grading. Downscale-only, onSubjectClipping='extract'.

Neutralize this dish to its own in-frame grey card and carry the shared house look: reason the white-balance/exposure from THIS frame's card to the shared white point, protecting the bright speculars from clipping, then apply the house tone. Report the settings applied.

Crop to the card dish-frame ratio, grey card cropped OUT; pre-crop master (coldbrew_neutral) retained for neutrality grading. All eight frames now share one white point, each neutralized to its own card. Downscale-only, onSubjectClipping='extract'.
Prep-before-trace step 1: the scan sits slightly rotated on the bed — straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drive the off-white paper toward clean white so the inked lettering separates hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). The enclosed counters remain filled with the crisped ground, which is why the masthead is a light cream panel where they read correctly.

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent ground) into a clean SVG for the masthead. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids.

Initialize an upload session for the eight grey-card-neutralized dish assets (the flagship as a transparent PNG, the rest as matched crops), the vector wordmark, and the licensed chalkboard texture, uploaded under the exact names the roster's @dish/@wordmark/@texture columns reference so the merge can resolve them. Plumbing, not difficulty.

Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's @dish (per-row photo), @wordmark (shared vector mark) and @texture (shared chalkboard) columns resolve to for each single-record card's frames.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the eight roster rows (section/item/desc/price) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live <<fields>> and resolve ALL THREE image columns per row — drop that row's graded photo into the @dish frame, the shared vectorized wordmark into the masthead via @wordmark, and the shared chalkboard texture into the full-bleed background via @texture — producing EXACTLY ONE merged card per row (eight cards). Binding the wordmark and texture through image columns is the only connector-doable path since free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned. [T] requires the hand-authored template with its three merge-wired image frames. A multi-item one-page grid is impossible here, and a convert_pdf_to_indd template would not bind — both are avoided.

Export the merged single-record cards to a press-ready ~300 DPI PDF, one card per dish. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document (all eight cards, one page per dish) in a single call — it cannot export one named record on its own, so the flagship Double Smash is simply page 1 of this set, not a separate file. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 8; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining throughout. The chalkboard texture chains asset_search(1) -> asset_license_and_download_stock(2). Eight per-dish grade sub-chains fan out from the raw captures, each an image_apply_adjustments neutralization driven to that frame's own in-frame 18% grey card so all eight converge on one shared warm street-food white point, followed by a card-frame crop, with image_auto_straighten inserted only on the tilted frames. The flagship runs the deepest branch: auto_straighten(3) -> apply_adjustments neutralize+house-look(4) -> select_by_prompt sauce(5) -> masked adjust_hsl sauce recolor(6) -> select_subject(7) -> masked apply_adjustments local lift(8) -> crop(9) -> remove_background to transparency(10), producing the transparent @dish for row 1. The other seven each run neutralize -> crop (single_classic 11-12, bacon with a straighten 13-15, mushroom 16-17, fries with a straighten 18-20, onion 21-22, cola 23-24, cold brew 25-26), every neutralization reasoned to its own card and every pre-crop *_neutral master retained (card in frame) as the neutrality-grading artifact while the *_crop (card removed) binds into the card. The wordmark runs a genuine prep-before-trace chain: auto_straighten(27) -> apply_adjustments crisp(28) -> crop_to_bounds(29) -> remove_background to transparency(30) -> vectorize(31).
